name: Terminal Portfolio
tagline: The site you're looking at — a dependency-free terminal in the browser.
what: A keyboard-driven portfolio that renders like a shell. Commands are ES modules, content lives in JSON, and everything is clickable so it works without typing.
hard: Keeping it framework-free while staying discoverable — every command output doubles as clickable navigation.
highlights: No build step, no dependencies — just static files.
Tab completion, command history, and did-you-mean suggestions.

name: Telemetry Monitor
tagline: Real-time decoding and visualization of binary packet streams from embedded hardware. Built for a defense internship so I can't share the codebase.
what: A desktop tool that ingests binary telemetry over TCP/UDP, decodes it against a user-defined packet schema, and renders a live KPI dashboard with per-channel plotting and a full CRC integrity pipeline.
hard: Achieving thread-safe packet ingestion at 4000+ packets/sec with >1000 bytes per packet without dropping frames or blocking the UI.
highlights: User-defined packet schema editor with preset and custom CRC algorithms.
Singleton service architecture with dedicated subservices for ingestion and connection management.
Auto-expanding KPI tiles and per-channel live plots.

name: RNA Thermosensor Designer
tagline: Feedback design pipeline to evolve RNA sequences that melt at a target temperature.
what: A computational pipeline that runs N independent NUAD searches to produce RNA thermosensor candidates. Each run mutates sequences via Hamming-distance steps scored against a constraint set covering GC composition, loop size, stem length, and Kozak exposure probability.
hard: Combining structural constraints (stem/loop geometry, GC balance) with a thermodynamic objective (Kozak exposure probability at a target Tm) into a single differentiable score that NUAD can minimize without the runs collapsing to the same local optimum.
highlights: Multi-run search with per-run RNG seeds for sequence diversity and deduplication.
Custom NUAD constraint classes for stem length, loop size, GC composition, and Kozak exposure.
Exposure probability computed via NUPACK ensemble thermodynamics at the target melting temperature.

name: McMaster SynBio Website
tagline: Maintainer of the McMaster SynBio club's public site.
what: The public-facing site for McMaster SynBio, built with the Next.js App Router and incrementally prerendered on Netlify. As one of the maintainers I handle feature work, content updates, and dependency upkeep on a live org site.
highlights: Next.js App Router with incremental static regeneration (ISR) on Netlify.
Ongoing maintenance: features, content, and dependency upkeep on a production site.

name: iGEM 2025 Wiki — Sterosaurus
tagline: McMaster's iGEM 2025 project wiki, hardened for iGEM's archival subpath hosting. Live at 2025.igem.wiki/mcmasteru.
what: The public wiki documenting McMaster's iGEM 2025 project. A Next.js static export deployed through iGEM's own GitLab CI/CD, where every team's site is served under a fixed subpath and archived permanently for judging.
hard: iGEM runs the site under a non-root subpath (/mcmasteru/) on their infrastructure with no server. Getting a Next.js export to resolve every asset, route, and image under that basePath — and publish cleanly through their GitLab pipeline — was most of the work.
highlights: Configured Next.js basePath/assetPrefix so the whole app runs under /mcmasteru/.
Static export with no SSR, so the wiki stays self-contained and archivable.
Set up the GitLab CI/CD pipeline to build and publish on push.

name: Ergosterol Overproduction in C. reinhardtii
tagline: Genome-scale metabolic modelling for ergosterol overproduction — the compbio core of McMaster's iGEM 2025. Accepted as an abstract to ALGS 2026 (Elsevier).
what: Gap-fills the genome-scale metabolic model iCre1355 (Chlamydomonas reinhardtii) with a heterologous ergosterol pathway, then uses flux-balance analysis to test strategies for overproducing it — squalene synthase (SQS) and squalene epoxidase (SQE) overexpression plus the mevalonate (MVA) pathway, across multiple donor strains.
hard: Gap-filling a model that was never built for sterol biosynthesis: adding the ergosterol pathway to iCre1355 and getting FBA/FVA/GECKO to return feasible, biologically meaningful flux across 24 heterologous constructs and three trophic conditions — instead of the model routing around the change or collapsing to degenerate optima.
highlights: Accepted as an abstract to ALGS 2026 (Elsevier).
Gap-filled iCre1355 under autotrophic, heterotrophic, and mixotrophic conditions; benchmarked model quality with Memote.
Built and analyzed 24 heterologous constructs (SQS/SQE + MVA across donor strains) via FBA, pFBA, and FVA.
Enzyme-constrained GECKO modelling and sensitivity analysis, with pathway maps rendered in Escher.

name: Epigenetic Markers of Memory Loss
tagline: Predicting Alzheimer's risk and cognitive decline from DNA methylation profiles. Built at the HackBio hackathon.
what: An end-to-end pipeline that predicts cognitive impairment from blood DNA-methylation data: EWAS feature selection over CpG sites, XGBoost and PyTorch (ConvNet/MLP) classifiers, SHAP for interpretability, all served by a FastAPI backend behind a Next.js dashboard.
hard: Methylation data is wide and shallow — hundreds of thousands of CpG features against only a few hundred samples. Selecting disease-associated sites (EWAS) and regularizing the models hard enough to generalize instead of memorize was the whole game.
highlights: EWAS feature selection to surface disease-associated CpG sites and genes.
XGBoost and PyTorch models with cross-validation; SHAP for per-prediction interpretability.
FastAPI inference backend serving a Next.js + Tailwind dashboard (ROC, SHAP, feature importance).

name: Lab Inventory Management System
tagline: Inventory, orders, and task delegation for a synthetic-biology team.
what: A full-stack LIMS built for McMaster SynBio to manage lab inventory, orders, and task assignment, with server-side rendering and a uniform terminal-adjacent design.
hard: Modelling row-level security so members only see what they should while keeping the schema simple enough to maintain.
highlights: Supabase backend with RLS policies and authentication.
Next.js + TypeScript frontend with server-side components for fast routing.

name: Shunting-Yard Math Compiler
tagline: A C program that parses and evaluates string math expressions, with numerical calculus.
what: Evaluates arbitrary math expressions given as strings: the shunting-yard algorithm converts infix to Reverse Polish Notation using hand-rolled stack and queue structures, then evaluates it. Extends to numerical calculus — Riemann-sum integral approximation over two-variable functions.
hard: Writing the parser and evaluator from scratch in C with manual memory management — the Makefile ships gdb and Valgrind targets precisely because keeping the stack/queue lifecycle leak-free was the tricky part.
highlights: Shunting-yard infix-to-RPN conversion with a hand-rolled stack and queue.
Riemann-sum integral approximation for two-variable functions.
Makefile with test, debug (gdb), and leak-check (Valgrind) targets.
